help.intro: To compare, German adds -er to the adjective and joins the two things with als: Ein Zug ist schneller als ein Bus. That works for every adjective, long or short — there is no 'more interesting': interessanter. Many short adjectives with a, o or u take an umlaut (alt → älter, groß → größer, jung → jünger, warm → wärmer), and four are irregular in a way English speakers will recognise: gut → besser, viel → mehr, gern → lieber, hoch → höher. For 'as … as' use genauso … wie / so … wie. After sein the comparative takes no ending; before a noun it takes the adjective ending on top (ein schnellerer Zug — that comes later in the course).
help.tips[0].title: -er + als, for every adjective
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The film is more interesting than the book.
help.tips[0].trap: English uses 'more' for long adjectives. German never does — 'mehr interessant' is the tell-tale error.
help.tips[0].check.why: Every adjective, even a long one, just adds -er before als. German never uses mehr for this.
help.tips[1].title: Umlaut on many one-syllable a/o/u adjectives
help.tips[1].text: alt → älter, groß → größer, jung → jünger, warm → wärmer, kalt → kälter, lang → länger, kurz → kürzer, stark → stärker. But: langsam → langsamer (no umlaut on longer words).
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: My brother is older than me, but I am taller.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: In winter it's colder, and the days are shorter.
help.tips[1].check.q: Im Sommer sind die Tage ____ als im Winter.
help.tips[1].check.why: Short adjectives with a, o or u usually get an umlaut: lang → länger.
help.tips[2].title: The irregular four — and teuer
help.tips[2].text: gut → besser, viel → mehr, gern → lieber, hoch → höher. And teuer drops an e: teurer; dunkel → dunkler.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: I prefer tea to coffee. The car is more expensive than the bike.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: My room is darker than yours.
help.tips[2].check.why: gut is irregular: gut → besser, just like good → better in English.
help.tips[3].title: as … as: genauso … wie
help.tips[3].text: Sie ist genauso alt wie ich. Not als — wie. als is for a difference, wie for equality.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: The bike is not as fast as the car.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: My brother is just as tall as my father.
help.tips[3].check.q: Mein Auto ist genauso alt ____ deins.
help.tips[3].check.why: Equality takes wie: genauso … wie. als is only for a difference (älter als).
help.remember[1]: gut–besser, viel–mehr, gern–lieber: the three you already half know from English.
help.context.en: Shall we go by train or by car? – The train is faster than the car, but the car is cheaper. – And more comfortable? – The train is just as comfortable as the car, and on the train I can read. I'd rather do that than drive. – Fine, the train then. It's better for the environment.
help.mistakes[1].why: A difference takes als; wie is for equality.
help.hook: Train or car, Berlin or Bonn, tea or coffee: one ending, -er, plus als lets you compare almost anything.
help.table.caption: Three steps
sentences[0].english: A train is faster than a bus.
sentences[0].why: The comparative adds -er: schneller — and the comparison word is als, never wie.
sentences[1].english: My brother is older than me.
sentences[1].why: Short a/o/u adjectives take an umlaut: alt → älter.
sentences[3].english: Today it is warmer than yesterday.
sentences[3].why: warm → wärmer — one of the umlaut comparatives.
sentences[4].english: This book is better than the film.
sentences[4].why: gut is irregular: besser — like good/better.
sentences[5].why: gern's comparative is lieber — preferring is 'doing more gladly'.
sentences[6].english: A bike is slower than a car.
sentences[6].why: langsam just adds -er: langsamer — no umlaut on long or two-syllable stems.
sentences[7].english: In winter the days are shorter than in summer.
sentences[8].english: My sister is younger than me.
sentences[8].why: jung → jünger — the u takes an umlaut.
sentences[9].english: I eat more fruit than sweets.
sentences[9].why: viel is irregular: mehr — like much/more.
sentences[11].english: The hotel is more expensive than the youth hostel.
sentences[11].why: teuer drops an e before -er: teurer.
sentences[12].english: My new phone is lighter than the old one.
sentences[12].why: leicht + -er = leichter — ei never takes an umlaut.
sentences[13].english: The flat is smaller than the house.
sentences[14].english: In summer the days are longer than in winter.
sentences[15].english: When it rains I'd rather take the bus than cycle.
